pillar_1.name: Seek Truth and Report It
pillar_1.description: Ethical journalism treats truth as a cornerstone. It holds accuracy above all else and is transparent about uncertainty.

headline_fidelity.description: Does the headline accurately represent the article body? Sensationalized or misleading headlines that overstate findings are flagged.

attribution_patterns.description: How frequently are factual claims attributed to named, on-record sources? Anonymous sourcing is noted; unattributed factual claims are flagged.

hedging_language.description: Does the journalist appropriately use hedging language (alleged, accused, reportedly) when facts are not established?

pillar_2.name: Minimize Harm
pillar_2.description: Ethical journalism treats sources, subjects, colleagues, and members of the public as human beings deserving of respect.

language_patterns.description: Does word choice dehumanize, stigmatize, or inflame? Patterns across the corpus are analyzed — single instances are not scored.

sentiment_differential.description: Is there a statistically significant difference in tone or word choice when covering politically opposed subjects?

pillar_3.name: Act Independently
pillar_3.description: Ethical journalism means avoiding conflicts of interest, real or perceived. Journalists owe allegiance to the public, not to sources, advertisers, or political actors.

financial_conflicts.description: FEC records are checked for political contributions. Contributions are reported as fact; the scoring reflects the degree of conflict with covered subjects.

source_diversity.description: Across the corpus, how diverse is the range of sources cited? Overreliance on a narrow set of affiliated sources is flagged.

social_media_independence.description: Do public social posts reveal advocacy for political positions or causes that may conflict with independent reporting?

pillar_4.name: Be Accountable and Transparent
pillar_4.description: Ethical journalism means acknowledging errors promptly and explaining news judgments. Accountability is demonstrated through the corrections record.

corrections_frequency.description: How often are corrections issued relative to corpus size?

corrections_velocity.description: How quickly are corrections issued after errors are identified?

corrections_severity.description: What is the nature of corrections? Factual errors carry more weight than clarifications.

data_sufficiency.note: Dimensions are not scored until minimum corpus thresholds are met. Profiles are published with placeholder status until all pillar thresholds are satisfied.

statuses.collecting: Data collection in progress. No score is shown.
statuses.insufficient: Data collected but below minimum threshold for this dimension. Marked as insufficient data rather than scored.
statuses.scored: Minimum threshold met. Score is published with full citation trail.
